Call or send the form: which is faster?

A call is the fastest way in. It is transferred straight to a pool company, and if it cannot pick up, it gets your details for a call back. The form is there for when a call is not convenient: a local company calls you back once it has your request.

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (623) 240-0428 day or night, weekends included.
  2. Describe the poolSay what is going on: cloudy or green water, a pump that hums, a heater that will not fire, scale on the tile, and which part of the Valley you are in.
  3. Get put throughThe call is transferred to an independent, locally owned pool service company, which hears a short summary of the problem before it picks up.
  4. Deal with them directlyThat company looks at the pool, quotes, does the work and bills you. If it cannot answer, your name, number, area and problem are passed along so it can call you back.

Not sure what to say? Start with what you see

You do not need pool vocabulary. "The water turned green after the storm," "the pump hums but nothing moves," or "the heater clicks and shuts off" is plenty. If the pump or heater is making a burning smell or tripping a breaker, turn it off at the controller or breaker and leave it off until a technician looks. If you smell gas near the heater, get away from it first and call 911 and Southwest Gas from a safe place.

Common questions

Is there an email address or contact form?

There is no public email address, but there is a short form on this page. Send your name, phone number, city or ZIP code and what the pool needs, and the request is passed to an independent local pool company that calls you back. For anything urgent, calling is faster: you are either transferred right away or your details are passed along for a call back.

What happens after I send the form?

Your request goes to the site owner, who passes it to an independent, locally owned pool service company that works in your area. That company calls you back to talk about the pool. Your details are not sold. If you do not hear back in a reasonable time, call the line.

What hours can I call?

Any hour. An automated assistant answers 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays. The pool company you reach sets its own hours for visits.

I already hired a company through the line and have a problem with the work. Who do I contact?

Contact the pool company directly, since it did the work and billed you. If the dispute is about contractor work and you cannot resolve it, the Arizona Registrar of Contractors accepts complaints against contractors, and its contractor search shows a company's license and complaint history.

The quickest way to help is still a phone call

One free call at any hour. Say what the pool is doing and where in the Valley you live, and the line puts you through to an independent, locally owned pool company that sees the pool for itself and sets its own price.

Call (623) 240-0428
